A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EMGauss work, with readable and matchable text, equations, figures and tables. Neither contains an appendix or the referenced supplementary materials. Consequently, supplementary anisotropy tests, v2's mentioned slice-bundle studies and its supplementary video cannot be compared.

before.justification: V1 reports original reconstruction experiments on EPFL, FIB-25 and FANC, quantitative comparisons in Table 3, and a teacher-student ablation in Table 4.

after.justification: V2 retains original reconstruction results and adds IsoVEM comparisons, downstream segmentation results and component ablations in Tables 2–4.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.4 and Algorithm 1 retain the same deformation model, fixed axial coordinates/scales, dynamic opacity, time-independent rotation, EMA teacher, losses and three-stage training procedure. The additional ablations test existing components rather than introduce a revised method.

E1.justification: EPFL, FIB-25 and FANC remain the reconstruction datasets. V2 adds downstream cellular segmentation on reconstructed EPFL sequences in Section 4.4, extending task coverage within the existing data domain.

E2.justification: IsoVEM, previously only cited, is newly evaluated on EPFL and FIB-25 in v2 Table 2. CycleGAN-IR and EMDiffuse remain reconstruction comparators. The separate training-cost comparison involving those baselines in v1 Table 2 is removed.

E3.justification: V2 introduces SAM2 segmentation with IoU evaluation on EPFL at ×6 anisotropy and additional component-ablation conditions. Existing reconstruction volume sizes, subsampling, metrics and EMGauss training schedule remain unchanged. Removed descriptions of baseline training and checkpoint selection do not establish changed experimental execution.

E4.justification: Table 4 expands the single teacher-student ablation into an assessment of training stages and Gaussian configuration: removing warm-up, removing joint training, disabling dynamic opacity and enabling dynamic rotation. This substantially broadens the evidence for component choices. Both versions mention ×4/×8 tests, but their results and v2's mentioned slice-bundle analysis are unavailable in the supplied PDFs.

E5.justification: Neither PDF reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance testing. Table 4 continues to average results across two datasets, rather than report uncertainty across runs.

E6.justification: Retained reconstruction and teacher-student ablation scores are unchanged. V2 adds IsoVEM results, including EPFL/FIB-25 PSNR of 23.91/21.51, four component-ablation rows, and segmentation IoU of 0.9099/0.9555/0.9687 for CycleGAN-IR/EMDiffuse/EMGauss. Figure 5 also replaces the qualitative examples. Conversely, v1's training-cost results—2h/500 frames, 24h/128 frames and 0.5h/6 frames respectively—are removed.

T1.justification: The Gaussian definitions, covariance projection, deformation equations and axial constraints in Equations 1–6 are mathematically unchanged. Neither version adds theoretical propositions, proofs or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the central claims of continuous Gaussian-based reconstruction without isotropy assumptions or external isotropic training data. The conclusion modestly narrows its claimed benefits, dropping explicit noise suppression and the reference to artifacts from patch-based formulations.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations connecting omitted warm-up to coarse initialization and Gaussian proliferation, static opacity to noise during structural appearance/disappearance, and dynamic rotation to temporal jitter. It also interprets segmentation results as evidence of downstream structural utility. The main noise-related memory limitation remains.

D1.justification: V2 removes the specification that EMDiffuse uses another same-sized tissue volume, the statement that baseline codebase defaults are used, quantitative training-time/frame requirements, and the no-teacher ablation's best-iteration selection disclosure. EMGauss's optimizer, iteration schedule, EMA decay and GPU remain documented unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds the SAM2 reference and explicitly frames the evaluated baselines as GAN-, diffusion- and transformer-based approaches. IsoVEM was already cited in v1. The underlying positioning against isotropy-dependent reconstruction and relative to Gaussian-splatting research remains stable.

P1.justification: V2 rewrites related-work passages and streamlines experimental descriptions and the conclusion. It adds a downstream-segmentation subsection and acknowledgements, while retaining the overall section sequence and largely preserving the abstract, introduction and method narrative.

P2.justification: The document is comprehensively reformatted from single-column to two-column layout. Figure 1 is redrawn, Figure 5 replaces its original montage with two cropped comparisons, and other figures receive revised sizing and labels. The cost table is removed, a segmentation table is added, and reconstruction and ablation tables are expanded.

improvement.justification: V2 tests training-stage and Gaussian-design choices that v1 largely justified verbally, adds a transformer comparator, and connects reconstruction quality to downstream segmentation. These strengthen empirical support for the unchanged method. However, removal of the quantitative efficiency comparison and several reproducibility disclosures limits the gain; referenced supplementary evidence remains unavailable.
